body_markdown:
Rocket.new combines market research, competitive intelligence, and app building in a single platform, but its credit-based pricing model can make costs dependent on usage as projects grow. According to the 2026 Developer Survey,[65.9% of respondents](https://survey.stackoverflow.co/2026/ai/data/ai-select) use AI coding assistants or coding agents at work, highlighting the growing adoption of AI-assisted development. For founders and builders who already pay for Claude or ChatGPT, another AI-building subscription can add to development costs.


This guide examines nine Rocket.new alternatives and complementary workflows through the lens of cost predictability, infrastructure completeness, and workflow efficiency, helping non-technical founders, small business owners, and development teams find the right[AI app builder](https://floot.com/en) for their needs.


## **Key Takeaways**


- **Build through existing AI assistants** : Floot's[MCP connector](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Available actions depend on the connected client's permissions.
- **Daily building-action limits improve cost predictability** : Floot's[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) use daily building-action limits instead of separate AI credits for ordinary connector-based development. Hosting, optional AI features, and third-party services may incur additional charges.
- **Managed infrastructure reduces setup complexity** : Floot provides a PostgreSQL database, authentication, file storage, email, and[built-in hosting](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) , reducing the need to configure separate infrastructure services.
- **Mobile publishing extends web applications** : Floot can package web apps into native iOS and Android shells, with[mobile publishing](https://floot.com/en/mobile) workflows for testing and store submission. Developer accounts and store approval remain necessary.
- **Non-technical builders can focus on functionality** : Floot suits founders and business owners who need working applications with saved data, user accounts, and business workflows. Its[app-building guide](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) explains the infrastructure and deployment considerations.


## **Understanding AI App Builders**


AI app builders let users describe application requirements in natural language and receive generated interfaces, workflows, and application logic. They differ from traditional coding environments because users can request features conversationally instead of implementing every change manually. However, the level of backend support, hosting, deployment automation, and technical knowledge required varies by platform. Understanding these differences helps builders choose a solution that supports both initial development and ongoing operation.


The core requirements for effective AI app builders include:


- **Natural language development** : Describe features, functionality, and changes through conversation instead of writing code manually. Floot's[connector documentation](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) explains how supported AI assistants can interact with projects.
- **Managed infrastructure** : Access databases, authentication, storage, and hosting without configuring every service independently. Floot's[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) cover these components.
- **Deployment capabilities** : Publish working web applications and, where supported, prepare mobile applications for distribution through app stores.
- **Iteration and testing** : Make changes, inspect results, and debug applications through conversational workflows, with capabilities depending on the connected tools and permissions.
- **Cost predictability** : Understand subscription fees, development usage limits, hosting allowances, and additional service charges before expanding a project.


Rocket.new offers Solve and Intelligence capabilities alongside app building. Its free tier includes 20 one-time credits, while the $25/month Pro plan includes 100 monthly credits. Actual consumption depends on the number and complexity of development and research tasks.


The alternatives below take different approaches to these requirements. Some emphasize managed infrastructure, others prioritize code-level control, and some combine both. Pricing figures reflect publicly listed US-dollar plans checked in November 2026 and may change during 2027.


## **1. Floot**


[Floot](https://floot.com/en) is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that lets users create, edit, and publish applications through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. Floot provides managed infrastructure while the connected AI assistant handles development, with available building capabilities depending on the client's connector permissions.


Instead of requiring users to adopt another AI-building interface, Floot supports development through familiar assistants while providing the backend services needed to operate working applications.


### **Key Capabilities for App Building**


- **MCP connector integration** : Build apps[in Claude or ChatGPT](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) , Codex, Cursor, and other supported MCP clients without switching to a separate AI-building workflow
- **Complete managed infrastructure** : PostgreSQL database, user authentication, file storage, and[built-in services](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) available for application development and hosting
- **Native email and notifications** : Built-in transactional email without requiring a separate email provider; sending emails to customers requires a verified sending domain and a paid Floot plan
- **Scheduled tasks** : Recurring jobs without external schedulers, available for published apps while the project owner has a paid plan
- **Mobile app conversion** : Package web apps in native iOS and Android shells, with[mobile workflows](https://floot.com/en/mobile) for testing and store submission, subject to developer-account requirements and store review


### **Use Cases and Workflow**


Floot supports multiple application types. For MVPs and prototypes, founders can describe their product in conversation while a supported AI assistant develops the application using Floot's database, authentication, and hosting services. Internal tools for small businesses can include employee portals, inventory systems, and customer management applications without requiring owners to manage infrastructure.


E-commerce applications can use integrated Stripe payments alongside shipping rates, labels, and order tracking through Shippo. Live Stripe payments require a Pro or Power Floot plan and a connected Stripe account. Stripe processing fees apply, along with a 1% Floot transaction fee on Pro and 0% on Power. Real shipping labels require a Shippo account, with shipping charges billed by Shippo.


Floot holds a 4.8/5 rating on G2 based on eight user reviews at the time of checking in November 2026. Reviewers have highlighted ease of use, transparent troubleshooting, and support responsiveness, although the review sample remains small.


### **Pricing Structure**


Floot is free to start and offers three plans. Based on its[pricing page](https://floot.com/en/pricing) , the current US-dollar subscription prices and core allowances are:


- **Free** : $0/month, 100 building actions/day, 3,000 one-time starter AI credits, and a one-time $3 hosting allowance
- **Pro** : $25/month, 1,000 building actions/day, 5,000 monthly AI credits, $10 monthly hosting allowance, and custom-domain support
- **Power** : $100/month, 5,000 building actions/day, 15,000 monthly AI credits, $25 monthly hosting allowance, and additional capacity for high-volume building


Floot's newer mobile documentation lists 2 monthly mobile builds on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Google Play account connections require a paid Floot plan, while Apple connections are available on every plan.


Failed building actions do not count against daily limits. Hosting beyond the included allowance is usage-billed and can use prepaid hosting credits. Optional AI features, external integrations, and third-party services may create additional costs.


Users retain ownership of their code and data on every plan, while downloading the project code as a ZIP requires a paid plan. Details are available in Floot's[code export documentation](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) .


### **Why Floot Leads for AI App Building**


Unlike platforms that bundle their own AI-building credit systems, Floot's connector workflow uses the user's existing supported AI assistant for ordinary development. This avoids a separate Floot AI build-credit charge for connector-based actions, although users still pay for their AI subscription, applicable Floot plan, hosting usage, and optional services.


Floot AI credits apply to features such as its optional in-editor AI agent, image generation, and AI functionality inside published apps. Connector building uses daily building actions, with image generation also consuming credits when applicable.


Its[MCP integration](https://floot.com/blog/what-is-mcp-a-simple-guide-to-model-context-protocol-for-ai-apps) allows supported assistants to access Floot tools and project context according to their permissions. Development can happen through conversation, while Floot manages the application's database, authentication, storage, and hosting. The time required to build and publish depends on project complexity, integrations, and testing requirements.


## **2. Lovable**


Lovable, formerly GPT Engineer, focuses on full-stack web application development with generated code, managed backend services, and GitHub synchronization.


### **Primary Focus**


- **GitHub synchronization** : Synchronize application code with GitHub for version control and continued development
- **React and TypeScript stack** : Generate web applications using modern frontend technologies
- **Managed backend** : Database, authentication, and hosting through Lovable Cloud, with support for connecting Supabase
- **Code ownership** : Access generated code and continue development outside the platform
- **Web application focus** : Designed primarily for browser-based applications


### **Organizational Fit**


Lovable suits teams that prioritize code ownership and want the option to continue development using GitHub and external infrastructure. Its synchronization workflow can appeal to organizations with existing version-control practices. Teams focused on web applications may find this approach aligned with their requirements.


For a broader comparison of application-building workflows, see Floot's[Lovable alternatives guide](https://floot.com/blog/best-lovable-alternatives-in-2026-apps-that-can-actually-ship) .


### **Pricing**


Lovable offers a Free plan with daily build-credit grants subject to a monthly cap. Its Pro plan costs $25/month and includes 100 monthly credits, alongside applicable daily and Cloud grants. Credit use varies by task complexity, and additional credits or hosting usage may affect overall spending.


## **3. Bolt.new**


Bolt.new operates as a browser-based development environment by StackBlitz, offering real-time previews and a free tier for prototyping.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Browser-based IDE** : No local setup required for development
- **Real-time preview** : Immediate visual feedback as changes are made
- **Free development allowance** : 1 million tokens per month, with a 300,000 daily token limit
- **Bolt Cloud** : Integrated backend services that users can configure as needed
- **GitHub integration** : Code synchronization and version control


### **Organizational Fit**


Bolt.new fits teams focused on prototyping and experimentation who want to minimize initial setup. Its browser-based approach removes the need for a local development environment, while Bolt Cloud provides integrated backend services.


Teams comfortable with token-based usage may find the free allowance useful for testing ideas. For another perspective on workflow and infrastructure differences, see Floot's[Bolt comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-bolt-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


### **Pricing**


Bolt.new offers a Free plan with 1 million monthly tokens and a 300,000 daily limit. Pro costs $25/month when billed monthly and starts at 10 million tokens per month, without a daily token limit. Higher usage requirements and team features may involve different plans or costs.


## **4. Replit**


Replit, founded in 2016, offers a cloud development environment with AI assistance across a wide range of programming languages.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Full IDE capabilities** : Development environment with debugging and testing tools
- **Multi-language support** : Supports numerous programming languages beyond web technologies
- **AI Agent** : Built-in AI assistance for generating and modifying applications
- **Collaboration features** : Shared workspaces and team development capabilities
- **Deployment options** : Hosting for applications built on the platform


### **Organizational Fit**


Replit appeals to developers who want AI assistance within a coding environment. The platform supports natural-language app building through Replit Agent while also providing a traditional development interface for users who want direct access to their code.


Teams working across multiple programming languages may find this flexibility useful. Floot's[Replit comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-replit-compare-ai-vibecoding-platforms-in-2026) provides additional context for evaluating managed infrastructure and development workflows.


### **Pricing**


Replit offers a Free starting option with limited usage. Its Core plan is listed at $20/month with monthly billing, or an effective $18/month when billed annually, and includes an allowance for supported AI model usage. Agent activity and deployment can generate additional usage-based charges depending on the plan and workload.


## **5. Base44**


Base44 offers an all-in-one managed app-building platform that Wix acquired in June 2025 for approximately $80 million in initial consideration, plus contingent earn-out payments. The acquisition brought AI app-building capabilities into the Wix product portfolio.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Managed infrastructure** : Database, authentication, and hosting included
- **AI-led building** : Natural language interface for application development
- **Wix ownership** : Part of the broader Wix product family
- **Application deployment** : Tools for moving generated applications from development to publishing
- **Business tool focus** : Supports internal tools and business applications


### **Organizational Fit**


Base44 may suit organizations seeking an integrated application-building environment. Teams evaluating the platform should consider its managed backend, credit-based development limits, available integrations, and long-term application requirements.


For more information on how these approaches differ, see Floot's[Base44 comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-base44-which-ai-app-builder-is-better-in-2026) .


### **Pricing**


Base44 offers a Free plan with limited message and integration credits. Its Starter plan costs $20/month with monthly billing, or an effective $16/month when billed annually, and includes 100 monthly message credits and 2,000 integration credits. Higher tiers provide larger allowances and additional development features.


## **6. Bubble**


Bubble represents the established visual app-builder category, combining drag-and-drop development, workflow tooling, and AI-assisted app-building capabilities.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Visual development** : Drag-and-drop interface for designing applications
- **Workflow tooling** : Logic and automation through visual configuration
- **Plugin ecosystem** : Marketplace for additional functionality
- **Established platform** : Long-running product with documentation and an active user community
- **Workload-based pricing** : Application operating costs scale according to workload consumption


### **Organizational Fit**


Bubble suits users who prefer visual development and direct control over application logic. Its interface requires users to learn the platform's workflow and data tools, but offers detailed control over application behavior.


Organizations with experience in visual development, or teams willing to learn Bubble's workflow model, may find it suitable for applications that require extensive customization.


### **Pricing**


Bubble offers a Free plan for building and testing applications. For web-only projects, its Starter plan costs $39/month with monthly billing, or an effective $32/month when billed annually. The plan includes a monthly workload-unit allowance, while higher consumption may require additional capacity. Mobile-only and combined web-and-mobile plans have separate pricing.


## **7. Cursor + Floot (Complementary Workflow)**


Cursor is an AI-assisted coding editor that supports MCP connections. When connected to Floot, it can provide a development workflow that combines IDE-based coding assistance with managed application infrastructure.


### **Primary Focus**


- **AI-assisted coding** : Code completion, generation, and editing within a desktop editor
- **MCP compatibility** : Supported clients can connect to Floot's managed application services
- **Developer-oriented** : Designed for users comfortable with code editors
- **Local development environment** : Files and editing tools remain accessible through the desktop application
- **Framework flexibility** : Supports different development languages and frameworks, while Floot projects follow Floot's supported application architecture


### **Organizational Fit**


Cursor with Floot fits teams that prefer IDE-based development while using managed database, authentication, storage, and hosting services. The combination can suit developers who want coding-tool control without configuring every backend service independently.


The available Floot operations depend on Cursor's MCP implementation, the connected account, and the permissions exposed to the client.


For more context, see Floot's[Cursor comparison](https://floot.com/blog/floot-vs-cursor-which-ai-development-tool-is-right-for-you-in-2026) .


### **Complementary Workflow**


Cursor addresses a different part of the development process from Rocket.new. It provides an AI-assisted coding environment rather than a standalone managed app-building platform. Connecting Cursor to Floot brings these workflows together, allowing developers to work in a familiar editor while using Floot for supported application-building operations and managed infrastructure.


This combination suits technical teams that value code-level interaction but want to reduce separate backend and deployment setup. Floot does not replace Cursor, and the connector does not guarantee that arbitrary existing codebases can be imported into Floot.


### **Pricing**


Cursor offers a Free plan with limited usage. Its newer subscription structure includes Plus at $8/month and Premium at $30/month, with additional tiers for higher usage. Legacy Cursor subscriptions may have different pricing and allowances.


Cursor and Floot subscriptions are separate. Users can start with Floot's Free plan, while the cost of their Cursor plan, AI model usage, and Floot infrastructure depends on their chosen configuration.


## **8. v0 by Vercel**


v0 is Vercel's AI app builder for generating interfaces and full-stack applications from natural language descriptions, with deployment through Vercel.


### **Primary Focus**


- **UI generation** : Creates React components from text descriptions
- **Vercel ecosystem** : Integrates with Vercel deployment and hosting
- **Full-stack development** : Supports complete web applications alongside individual UI components
- **Design iteration** : Tools for prototyping and refining interfaces
- **Framework integration** : Works within Next.js and React projects


### **Organizational Fit**


v0 suits teams that need UI prototyping or application development within the Vercel ecosystem. It supports interface generation and full-stack application development, with additional configuration depending on the project's backend and deployment needs.


Organizations already using Vercel may find the integrated deployment workflow useful when evaluating their development options.


### **Pricing**


v0 offers a Free plan with a limit of seven messages per day. Its Plus plan costs $30 per user/month and includes $30 in monthly credits, while Business costs $100 per user/month with additional controls. Additional usage and Vercel hosting charges may apply depending on the project.


## **9. ChatGPT Sites**


ChatGPT Sites lets eligible ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users create, host, and share websites and lightweight web applications directly through ChatGPT. Users can describe what they want, preview the result, refine it through conversation, and publish a hosted Site without configuring a separate deployment environment.


### **Primary Focus**


- **Conversational website building** : Create and edit websites and lightweight web apps through ChatGPT
- **Built-in hosting** : Publish Sites to hosted URLs, with custom-domain support where available
- **Persistent data** : Supports database storage, uploaded files, and sign-in options for compatible applications
- **Connected apps** : Eligible workspaces can build experiences that use visitors' authorized connected services
- **Usage-based limits** : Building and editing count toward Codex usage, while hosting and storage have separate allowances and limits


### **Organizational Fit**


ChatGPT Sites suits individuals and teams that want to create and share hosted web experiences directly within ChatGPT. It is useful for dashboards, internal resources, interactive websites, and lightweight applications that fit its supported runtime and workspace permissions.


Floot may be more appropriate for users who want managed PostgreSQL infrastructure and a workflow that can operate through Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. It also offers mobile application packaging and store-submission workflows.


The best choice depends on the required infrastructure, deployment environment, and preferred AI development workflow.


### **Pricing**


ChatGPT Sites is available through eligible paid ChatGPT subscriptions, including Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise. Building and editing count toward Codex usage, while hosting has separate usage allowances.


Hosting is included through December 31, 2026. Starting January 1, 2027, Plus, Pro, and Business customers are scheduled to pay for hosting consumption above their monthly allowances. Enterprise billing follows applicable workspace agreements. Custom domains and persistent storage can also affect hosting usage.


## **Why Floot Stands Out as the Top Rocket.new Alternative**


Floot is a practical choice for founders and business owners who already use supported AI assistants and want to turn application ideas into working products without managing separate infrastructure. Its full-stack platform combines[MCP-based development](https://floot.com/integrations/mcp) with managed services, while daily building-action limits help users understand development capacity.


Its main advantages include:


- **Familiar development workflow** : Build through supported AI assistants without adopting another dedicated AI-building interface
- **Managed application services** : Access PostgreSQL, authentication, file storage, email, and hosting through one platform
- **Clear development allowances** : Use daily building actions rather than separate Floot AI credits for ordinary connector development
- **Mobile publishing options** : Convert web projects into iOS and Android applications with supported store-testing workflows
- **Code and data ownership** : Retain ownership of application assets, with project ZIP exports available on paid plans


For[non-technical founders](https://floot.com/blog/best-ai-app-builders-for-non-technical-founders-in-2026) , Floot provides a way to create useful software while reducing infrastructure setup. Its[pricing plans](https://floot.com/en/pricing) are free to start, with hosting usage and optional services billed according to their applicable allowances.


## **Frequently Asked Questions**


### **What makes Floot different from other AI app builders?**


Floot is a full-stack app-building platform with an MCP connector that works through supported AI assistants, including Claude, Codex, Cursor, and compatible ChatGPT configurations. The connected assistant handles development while Floot provides managed infrastructure, including databases, authentication, storage, and hosting. This lets users work through familiar AI tools rather than adopting a separate AI-building interface. Available operations depend on the connected client's permissions. Floot's[MCP connector guide](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/build-from-claude-and-chatgpt) explains how this workflow operates.


### **Can I build mobile apps with AI app builders?**


Yes, although capabilities and publishing requirements vary by platform. Floot packages web applications into native iOS and Android shells and supports workflows for TestFlight and Google Play testing. Its newer documentation lists 2 monthly builds on Free, 12 on Pro, and unlimited builds on Power. Floot-managed store-testing uploads do not require a Mac or Xcode, although building downloaded iOS projects yourself does. Apple Developer Program membership costs $99 per year, and Google Play registration has a one-time $25 fee. Google Play connections also require a paid Floot plan. Final store approval is not guaranteed. See Floot's[mobile app guide](https://floot.com/en/mobile) .


### **How do AI app builder pricing models compare?**


AI app builders charge through different combinations of subscriptions, credits, tokens, development actions, and hosting usage. Floot's[pricing structure](https://floot.com/en/pricing) provides 100 daily building actions on Free, 1,000 on Pro, and 5,000 on Power. Ordinary connector-based building uses the user's existing AI subscription rather than separate Floot AI build credits. Hosting beyond included allowances, optional AI features, and third-party services can incur additional charges. Rocket.new, Lovable, and Base44 use credits, while Bolt.new primarily uses token allowances.


### **What infrastructure does Floot include?**


Floot includes a managed PostgreSQL database, user authentication, file storage, transactional email, backend services, and hosting. It also supports scheduled jobs, payments, and integrations, although some live capabilities require paid plans or external service accounts. Customer-facing email needs a verified sending domain, and live Stripe payments require a paid Floot plan. These capabilities can reduce the number of services founders need to configure independently. Floot's[built-in services documentation](https://floot.com/docs/integrations/whats-built-in) explains the available infrastructure.


### **Can I switch from another AI app builder to Floot?**


Yes, but migration depends on the existing application's code, data, architecture, and integrations. Floot does not directly import arbitrary external codebases, so moving from another builder may involve recreating the application through a supported AI assistant. Existing data, designs, and content can inform the rebuild, while authentication and third-party connections may need reconfiguration. Floot users retain ownership of their code and data, with project ZIP exports available on paid plans. See the[code export guide](https://floot.com/docs/faqs/code-data-and-exports) for ownership and migration considerations.
